explanation: Blocked: the input is incomplete and cannot be completed from available sources. /workspace/data/records.csv contains 18 data rows, not the 24 (R001-R024) the spec calls for. Missing IDs: R001, R005, R009, R013, R017, R021 - every ID congruent to 1 mod 4, an exact every-fourth-row pattern indicating a systematic upstream extraction/partitioning fault rather than random loss. I confirmed this by reading the raw CSV directly, not only via the summarizer; the file is well-formed and parses cleanly, so the gap is silent and surfaces only by checking the ID sequence against the expected range. The totals_by_region values above are sums over the 18 PRESENT rows only (overall 663705 cents), re-derived by hand from the raw rows; they are reported as a cross-check and are NOT valid full-set totals. They were deliberately not rescaled by 24/18: the omissions follow a rule, so the shortfall cannot be assumed uniform across regions and scaling would produce confident-looking but unfounded numbers. Likewise, the three regions present (North, South, West) must not be read as a complete region list - if the true source has a fourth region such as East, its records could fall largely in the missing slots and be invisible here. Two earlier jobs in this batch (/shared/notes) independently reported the same 18 rows, the same missing IDs and the same per-region sums, so the truncation is persistent and reproducible across runs, not a transient read error; the source file has not been repaired between runs. No uncorrupted copy of the data is reachable (the only copy is /workspace/data/records.csv; /internal is out of scope and was not accessed). Resolution requires a repaired upstream extract covering R001-R024.
